messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@aurorahealth.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: waiver for overrun during beta launch

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the fast turn-up last week — the team at Aurora appreciated the support. We ran into an unexpected traffic spike during our pilot launch window (third-party referral traffic routed to our UI), which pushed us well past the burst threshold. We received an overrun notice yesterday for ~$18,400.

We're still in a closed beta and this launch was explicitly to validate integration with Redwood's streaming API. Given the experimental nature and the fact this was a short abnormal window (about 3 hours), we'd like to request an overrun waiver or substantial credit for this incident. In exchange, Aurora is willing to:

- Participate in a Redwood customer case study (product page + short video) within 60 days
- Provide a written referral and intro to two prospective customers in our healthtech network
- Remain on the product beta program and provide prioritized feedback for the next 3 months

Attached is a usage extract and a short timeline of the spike (burst-usage-report.csv). We're also asking for the invoice to be held while we resolve this.

Can you advise whether Redwood can credit this overrun or put the invoice on hold while we work through a resolution? This is a small but painful cost for a pilot customer and would really help momentum.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Integrations
Aurora Health

(attachment: burst-usage-report.csv, CSV, 48KB)

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: waiver for overrun during beta launch

Folks — forwarding Aurora's ask. Summary below and need guidance on what we can commit without legal signoff.

Summary:
- Customer: Aurora Health (closed beta)
- Incident: ~3 hour traffic spike, overrun charge ~$18.4k
- Ask: full waiver or substantial credit; invoice hold while resolved
- Offer from customer: case study, referral intros, continued beta participation

Options I'm considering:
1) Offer a one-time credit covering 50% of the overrun ($9.2k) in exchange for case study + referral + sign-off on a short MOU within 30 days.
2) Offer 100% credit but require Fast-Track beta agreement and a PO committing to minimal monthly usage for 6 months (higher risk).
3) Deny credit but provide a partial credit + 30-day invoice hold while they provide further evidence.

Questions:
- Finance: what level of credit can we approve without escalation? (Laura)
- Partnerships/BDR: is the referral + case study currency sufficient for a larger concession? (Karthik)
- Legal: will a simple MOU be enough to formalize the exchange? (Naomi)

I'm leaning to option 1 as a balanced play (customer goodwill + clear deliverable). Happy to take an alternate suggestion.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
